# FX Cache

How to use VERA's FX cache to copy VRAM four bytes at a time, including a write that masks some of the nibbles.

This page covers how the example sets the cache up. For the full behaviour of VERA FX, see the [VERA FX reference](https://github.com/X16Community/x16-docs/blob/master/X16%20Reference%20-%2010%20-%20VERA%20FX%20Reference.md).

## How to run it

Open the folder in VSCode and press `F5`. The program stops at a `.breakpoint` once the cache is filled. Open the VRAM viewer at `$1000` and expand *VERA FX* in the variables window to see the cache, then step over each write to `DATA1` and watch four bytes change at a time.

## Test data

`setup_testdata` writes `$01`, `$02`, `$03` and `$04` to VRAM at `$0000`, then points `DATA0` back at `$0000`.

## Setting up the cache

`cache_read_write` turns on cache fill and cache write in `FX_CTRL`, which is only visible when `DCSEL` is 2. Writing `0` to `FX_MULT` resets the cache's byte and nibble index.

<pre class="shiki"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">2</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> &#x3C;&#x3C;</span><span style="color:#FF79C6"> 1</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">         ; DCSEL = 2</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> CTRL</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">%01100000</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">      ; cache fill and cache write</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> FX_CTRL</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> FX_MULT         </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; byte and nibble index = 0</span></span></code></pre>

Then the two data ports are set up. `DATA1` writes to `$1000` with an increment of 4, as each cache write covers four bytes. `DATA0` reads from `$0000` with an increment of 1.

<pre class="shiki"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">1</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">              ; ADDRSEL = 1</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> CTRL</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">$30</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">            ; increment 4</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_H</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">$10</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_M         </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $01000</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_L</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> CTRL            </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; ADDRSEL = 0</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">$10</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">            ; increment 1</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_H</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_M         </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $00000</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> ADDRx_L</span></span></code></pre>

## Filling the cache

With cache fill on, each read from `DATA0` puts the byte into the cache and moves the cache index on. Four reads fill it with `$01 $02 $03 $04`.

<pre class="shiki"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    ldd</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA0</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    ldd</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA0</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    ldd</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA0</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    ldd</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA0</span></span></code></pre>

`ldd` is one of the 65c02's undocumented opcodes (`$dc`). It reads the address and throws the value away without changing any registers, which is all that's needed to trigger the read.

## Writing the cache

With cache write on, a write to `DATA1` stores all four cache bytes at a four byte aligned address, and the value written is a nibble mask instead of data. Each bit covers one nibble, two bits per byte, and a set bit means *don't* write that nibble.

<pre class="shiki"><code><span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA1           </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $1000 = 01 02 03 04</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    stz</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA1           </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $1004 = 01 02 03 04</span></span>
<span class="line"></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    lda</span><span style="color:#B5E853"> #</span><span style="color:#FF79C6">$f0</span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">            ; bits 4 to 7 set: don't write bytes 2 and 3</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA1           </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $1008 = 01 02, then the last two bytes are unchanged</span></span>
<span class="line"><span style="color:#B5E853">    sta</span><span style="color:#EAEAEA"> DATA1           </span><span style="color:#8F8F8F;font-style:italic">; $100c = 01 02, then the last two bytes are unchanged</span></span></code></pre>
